settings_original.name: Gemini Decision 1
settings_original.note: Google's Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1, launched 11 Nov 2026) through OpenRouter's System One route (/api/v1/systemone, model google/gemini-decision-1; replies name google/gemini-decision-1-20261111), pinned to its one provider, Google AI Studio, with fallbacks off (provider.only [google-ai-studio], allow_fallbacks false). List price $0.10 per million input tokens, no output tokens (openrouter.ai/google/gemini-decision-1 and aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing, 11 Nov 2026); latency includes OpenRouter's own time. One choice question per request with up to 255 options (the API's limit; longer lists split by the league's rule); context 262,144 tokens, refused with 400 above it, never cut: League 1's largest stored request (229 options, 57,539 bytes) was 26,133 input tokens at the smoke test. The API sorts option keys alphabetically (UTF-8 bytes) before evaluation, so the model reads the options in that order, not the seeded one (aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api#choice). OpenRouter answers some 429s (Google's per-tier token limit): retried as on every route.

guard.metered: the entrant and the paid opponents it is pinned against (BILLED); prices in the file
guard.enforced: runner `league --guard` (959a8a2, src/guard.rs): every request attempt reserved before it is sent, refused past the cap; every entrant reply's model and provider exactly the expected ones; a stop latches (no request, no league start, check refuses)

cost_basis.method: Each playable pair's billed cost in the original match: the paid opponent's recorded cost_usd (Fastino GLiDE: input tokens x $0.04/M), plus Gemini Decision 1's own recorded cost_usd (OpenRouter usage.cost, $0.10/M input); local setups and programs bill nothing. Enforced in the repeat by the run guard's ledger (spent + reserved in flight), not by stored turns.
cost_basis.cap_basis: Gemini Decision 1's entry cap: $5.00 (entrant + paid opponents; tools/v3/late-gemini-decision/start.sh), of which its guard recorded $1.1819 at the entry's end (workspace/late-gemini-decision/state/guard.log, 2026-11-11T22:12:14Z; it billed every late-entry match from #993, other entries' paid opponents included); the repeat's run guard (runner 959a8a2, `league --guard`) holds the entrant and the paid opponents to the remaining $3.8181: every request attempt is reserved at its worst case in one ledger before it is sent and refused when it would pass the cap (the runner refuses to send; run.sh's minute check of the ledger only reports and stops).

time.method: Sum of each playable pair's original match duration (start to finish; the originals ran several matches at once, so one at a time is about this or less), plus server starts.
time.server_starts: entrant: none (hosted); each local opponent 1-5 min (state logs of the originals)

gpu_plan.note: Gemini Decision 1 is hosted (no card of its own); its 8 local opponents run one at a time on a second card, OPP_GPU, with room for the largest (Clef, 53,144 MiB + 2,000), as in its original (bariton GPU 2, reservation r_82bfcd93782c).

differences: Name: '<original> [repeat 1]', a new players row; settings otherwise as the original's (the changed fields are listed under Settings); one match at a time, as the original (start.sh, max_matches 1).

Runner: the original ran dab6da5 (clean) for its first stage (#993-#1013) and 38024d6 (clean; map-check v2 and the raw_entries decoder) for its local stage (#1053-#1063), both on origin/main's runner line (ca112dc); the repeat runs 959a8a2 (branch pinned-late-gemini): the repeats' runner 0e66836 (late-reax line with the pinned-pairs change 4ca4f08 and admit) with those four runner commits cherry-picked (cb669a0) and the run guard (c13992f, 959a8a2: reply identity and the shared pre-send cap, used with --guard only). late-reax adds decision clients (reax, baselabs, drex, nace) and a budget ledger, which the run guard uses; requests, sampling (provider defaults, nothing set), the prompt version, option-order seed and rules are the same.

Map check: map-check v2 (a probability map that is not exactly the shown ids, finite in [0, 1], summing to 1 within 1e-6, stores no probabilities; the returned choice is still played) applies to every repeat pair; the original's first-stage pairs (#993-#1013, dab6da5) ran without it. Plays are not affected; a first-stage pair can store probabilities in the original where the repeat stores none.

Hosted model: Gemini Decision 1 is served by Google AI Studio through OpenRouter. The repeat accepts a reply only when it names the original's served model google/gemini-decision-1-20261111 and provider Google AI Studio (as all 1,704 original decisions did); a model served under that same name but changed behind it cannot be detected from here.

Route check: the original's guard re-checked OpenRouter's listing every minute (3 failures stopped it); the repeat checks it once before the first match (smoke) and, in the runner (run guard), the served identity of every entrant reply: model google/gemini-decision-1-20261111 and provider Google AI Studio exactly, or the guard latches and the league stops for good. Fallbacks stay off.

Cap: the original's $5 entry cap with $1.1819 recorded (a minute poll of stored turns); the repeat's run guard holds the entrant and paid opponents to the remaining $3.8181 before every request attempt (see cost_basis).
